source: Ported from the govbot witness-slip draft (state participation directory).

jurisdictions.name: Alabama
jurisdictions.how_to: Testify in person at the committee meeting, or email the committee chair named on the hearing notice. Alabama has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Alaska
jurisdictions.how_to: Send a Public Opinion Message (POM) to legislators about a bill, or sign up to testify when a committee schedules a hearing on it.

jurisdictions.name: Arizona
jurisdictions.how_to: Use the Legislature's Request to Speak (RTS) system: sign in, find the bill on an upcoming agenda, record whether you're for or against it, and ask to speak at the hearing if you want to.

jurisdictions.name: Arkansas
jurisdictions.how_to: Appear in person at the committee meeting, or write to the committee chair named on the meeting notice. Arkansas has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: California
jurisdictions.how_to: Send a position letter through the Legislature's position letter portal, or email the committee before the hearing, to register support, opposition or written testimony.

jurisdictions.name: Colorado
jurisdictions.how_to: When a committee posts a hearing, sign up on the Legislature's public testimony site to testify in person, remotely, or in writing.

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut
jurisdictions.how_to: Each hearing agenda says how to email or upload written testimony; send yours before the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Delaware
jurisdictions.how_to: House committees often take virtual public comment through the meeting calendar; in the Senate it depends on the committee, so check the meeting notice.

jurisdictions.name: District of Columbia
jurisdictions.how_to: Each DC Council hearing notice explains how to sign up as a witness and how to send written testimony; follow it before the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Florida
jurisdictions.how_to: Fill out an Appearance Request form (House or Senate) to speak in committee on a bill. It asks to appear in person.

jurisdictions.name: Georgia
jurisdictions.how_to: Testify in person at the hearing, or email the committee listed on the agenda. Georgia has no statewide online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Guam
jurisdictions.how_to: Read the hearing notice the Legislature posts, and send your comment on the bill to the committee before or at the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Hawaii
jurisdictions.how_to: Create an account on the Capitol website, then submit written testimony, or sign up to testify remotely, on the measure being heard.

jurisdictions.name: Idaho
jurisdictions.how_to: Each committee agenda has a link to sign up to testify remotely; you can also testify in person. Sign up once the hearing is posted.

jurisdictions.name: Illinois
jurisdictions.how_to: File a witness slip on my.ilga.gov once a bill is posted for a committee hearing: say you support it, oppose it or have no position, and whether you want to testify. Slips close when the hearing starts and are public.

jurisdictions.name: Indiana
jurisdictions.how_to: Fill out the Legislature's Appearance Form to ask to speak in committee on a bill.

jurisdictions.name: Iowa
jurisdictions.how_to: Subcommittee and public-hearing pages take written comments and remarks by Zoom; comments open when that meeting is posted.

jurisdictions.name: Kansas
jurisdictions.how_to: Email written testimony to the committee assistant named on the committee agenda before the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Kentucky
jurisdictions.how_to: Fill out the committee's Testimony Request form to ask to speak at a meeting.

jurisdictions.name: Louisiana
jurisdictions.how_to: Fill out a witness card in the committee room to testify or put your position on the record.

jurisdictions.name: Maine
jurisdictions.how_to: Use the Legislature's testimony form to send written testimony or sign up to testify by Zoom for a public hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Maryland
jurisdictions.how_to: Use the MyMGA portal on the General Assembly's site: sign up as a witness and upload written testimony for House and Senate hearings.

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts
jurisdictions.how_to: Email written testimony to the committee holding the hearing; some hearings also take remarks by Zoom (the hearing notice says).

jurisdictions.name: Michigan
jurisdictions.how_to: Testify in person at the committee meeting, or send written remarks to the committee clerk named on the meeting notice.

jurisdictions.name: Minnesota
jurisdictions.how_to: When a hearing is scheduled, the House or Senate committee posts how to testify and where to send written comments; follow those instructions.

jurisdictions.name: Mississippi
jurisdictions.how_to: Appear in person at the committee meeting, or write to the committee chair. Mississippi has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Missouri
jurisdictions.how_to: Use the House's online Witness Form or the Senate's Witness Registration System to record your position for a hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Montana
jurisdictions.how_to: Use the Legislature's Public Participation app to testify remotely, send written comment, or send a short message to a committee.

jurisdictions.name: Nebraska
jurisdictions.how_to: When a public hearing is set, submit a position comment on the bill through the Legislature's website.

jurisdictions.name: Nevada
jurisdictions.how_to: Submit comments and exhibits on bills through NELIS, the Legislature's online system, during session.

jurisdictions.name: New Hampshire
jurisdictions.how_to: Sign up from the General Court calendar to testify in person or remotely at a committee hearing.

jurisdictions.name: New Jersey
jurisdictions.how_to: Each committee agenda explains how to submit written testimony; send it before the meeting.

jurisdictions.name: New Mexico
jurisdictions.how_to: Sign up online as a witness for the committee hearing on the bill.

jurisdictions.name: New York
jurisdictions.how_to: The Senate and Assembly each collect written and in-person testimony for their hearings; the hearing notice says how.

jurisdictions.name: North Carolina
jurisdictions.how_to: Some committees take online public comment and practice varies by chair, so check the committee calendar. You can also write to the chair.

jurisdictions.name: North Dakota
jurisdictions.how_to: Submit written testimony for a hearing through the Legislature's website during session, where hearing documents are posted.

jurisdictions.name: Northern Mariana Islands
jurisdictions.how_to: Contact the committee or attend its hearing. The CNMI Legislature has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Ohio
jurisdictions.how_to: Fill out the witness slip attached to the committee notice to testify or record your position. The House uses a standard form; Senate committees vary.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma
jurisdictions.how_to: Testify in committee, or write to the committee chair. Oklahoma has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Oregon
jurisdictions.how_to: Register online as a witness once a public hearing is scheduled; registration usually closes 30 minutes before the hearing starts.

jurisdictions.name: Pennsylvania
jurisdictions.how_to: Email written testimony to the committee before the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Puerto Rico
jurisdictions.how_to: Submit written testimony (a ponencia) on the measure to the committee.

jurisdictions.name: Rhode Island
jurisdictions.how_to: Follow the hearing notice's instructions to send written testimony to the committee.

jurisdictions.name: South Carolina
jurisdictions.how_to: Appear at the committee meeting, or write to the chair listed on the agenda. South Carolina has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: South Dakota
jurisdictions.how_to: Send written comments to the committee; bills and hearing documents are on the Legislature's website during session.

jurisdictions.name: Tennessee
jurisdictions.how_to: Testify in committee, or contact the committee's members. Tennessee has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Texas
jurisdictions.how_to: In the House, use witness registration to record your position or ask to testify. In the Senate, the committee clerk handles witnesses.

jurisdictions.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
jurisdictions.how_to: Contact the committee to testify on a bill at its hearing.

jurisdictions.name: USA (Federal)
jurisdictions.how_to: Find the rule or notice on Regulations.gov and submit a comment before its deadline, or register for an agency's public hearing when one is offered. Comments are public.

jurisdictions.name: Utah
jurisdictions.how_to: Submit a public comment on the bill through the Legislature's website during session.

jurisdictions.name: Vermont
jurisdictions.how_to: Email written testimony to the committee; some committees also take remote remarks.

jurisdictions.name: Virginia
jurisdictions.how_to: Send written comments to the committee through the committee's page on Virginia's Legislative Information System, around the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Washington
jurisdictions.how_to: Use Committee Sign-In to register to testify or submit written comments, usually until 24 hours after the hearing starts.

jurisdictions.name: West Virginia
jurisdictions.how_to: Speak at the committee meeting, or write to the committee. West Virginia has no online comment form.

jurisdictions.name: Wisconsin
jurisdictions.how_to: Register for the public hearing and submit written testimony through the Legislature's website once a hearing is noticed.

jurisdictions.name: Wyoming
jurisdictions.how_to: Attend the committee meeting to speak, or write to the committee.

tips: Name the bill number (or the rule's docket number) so your input reaches the right item.
Say whether you support or oppose it, and why, in a few sentences from your own experience.
Send it before the deadline on the hearing notice: many forms close when the hearing starts.
What you submit is usually public record, including your name.
